original_question: Which type of heterophoria is considered a latent condition in which torsion occurs in the absence of appropriate visual stimuli?

final_qi.question: Which type of heterophoria is considered a latent condition in which torsion occurs in the absence of appropriate visual stimuli?
final_qi.search_keyword: latent heterophoria torsion absence visual stimuli
final_qi.long_answer: The condition described is cyclophoria, which is a latent form of heterophoria involving torsional misalignment. In cyclophoria, the eyes tend to rotate about the visual axis (torsion) when normal fusion is disrupted in the absence of appropriate visual stimuli. It is not apparent during binocular viewing because the visual system’s fusion mechanisms normally cancel this latent deviation. This phenomenon is an example of the oculomotor system’s capacity for adaptation, where the latent deviation only becomes evident when fusion is absent or the system is otherwise challenged.

candidate.long_answer: Latent torsional heterophoria is a type of heterophoria in which an abnormal torsional position of the eyes becomes apparent only under conditions where binocular vision is disrupted, meaning that the normal visual references that help maintain proper torsion are absent. This latent condition refers to a hidden misalignment, which is typically compensated for during normal viewing but becomes measurable when the eyes are dissociated, revealing the torsional deviation.
